item.title: The Distress in Software Is About To Get Worse
item.content:encoded:
The Daily Spark

Subscribe View All Sparks Financial Markets & Risk Dynamics

November 24, 2026

About the Author Torsten Slok

Partner, Chief Economist

EXPLORE MORE Want More Daily Spark? Daily data-driven analysis on the economy, inflation and capital markets.
  • "Global Equities" Is a US Tech Bet November 23, 2026
Share

Software is being hit by a double whammy of AI disruption and rates staying higher for longer.

As a result, yields on software loans have climbed above 13% and software equities have sold off, see the first two charts.

A key problem is that many software loans were underwritten in 2021-22 as seven-year term loans with minimal amortization, so the maturity wall will hit in 2028 and 2029, with a significant part rated B- or CCC, at a time when the Fed has started raising interest rates again, see the third chart.

This matters because software makes up a big part of the overall market. At its peak, the software sector made up over 30% of all buyout deal value, see the fourth chart.

item.title: Higher for Longer Makes High-Quality Credit More Attractive
item.content:encoded:
The Daily Spark

Subscribe View All Sparks Financial Markets & Risk Dynamics

November 20, 2026

About the Author Torsten Slok

Partner, Chief Economist

EXPLORE MORE Want More Daily Spark? Daily data-driven analysis on the economy, inflation and capital markets.
  • AI Spending Powers 65% of GDP Growth November 19, 2026
Share

The convergence in yields across asset classes is remarkable, see chart below.

The all-in yield on US investment-grade corporate bonds has moved up to around 6%, now at the top of the range. That is above the S&P 500 forward earnings yield of around 4.5% and above the implied cap rate on all-equity REITs of around 5.7%.

In other words, investors are now paid more to own high-quality credit than to own equities, and with a lot less volatility. The last time IG yields were this far above the S&P 500 earnings yield was in the early 2000s.

Even the 3-month Treasury yield, at around 4%, is now close to the S&P 500 earnings yield. With the AI trade wobbling and the equity risk premium compressed, the case for taking equity risk looks less compelling than it did a few years ago, while all-in yields in high-quality fixed income look increasingly attractive.

item.title: AI Spending Powers 65% of GDP Growth
item.content:encoded:
November 19, 2026

About the Author Torsten Slok

Partner, Chief Economist

Share

AI investment added roughly 1.3 percentage points to real GDP growth over the last three quarters, or about 65% of the roughly 2% cumulative growth, led by software and computers, see chart below. These are gross figures that do not net out imports, so the net boost in the national accounts is likely somewhat smaller.

The bottom line is that AI is the number one source of growth for the US economy, and anyone making statements about the 2027 outlook for equity and credit markets is implicitly making assumptions about the pace and magnitude of the AI data center buildout.
